  ADR-0013 review verdict CONCERNS. One compile defect (E1, trivial fix) and several non-blocking GDScript and 4.7.2 gotchas. No deprecated or changed post-cutoff API is misused. Every "probed 2026-10-29" claim (V1) reproduced on 4.7.2.stable.mono. This used project-local probes in C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/review-ADR-0013/ and its w/ subfolder, which has the ADR-0010 promoted warnings at level 2. Reproduced: bsearch tie semantics (for [1,3,3,3,7], bsearch(3) is 1 and bsearch(3,false) is 4); PackedInt32Array.insert and remove_at keep order; a 0xDEADBEEF element write reads -559038737 and masks to 3735928559; PackedInt64Array holds 1<<40; duplicate() of a packed array is independent; a typed Array[String] nested in a Dictionary stays typed (is_typed true, is Array[String] true) through var_to_bytes then bytes_to_var and through duplicate(true). Idiomatic for 4.7.2: a one-line "@abstract class_name X extends RefCounted" followed by "@abstract func ... -> T" with a trailing comment loads (ADR-0010 and ADR-0011 write the same port header on two lines or one). A stub that omits a return fails with "Not all code paths return a value" (plus "no static return type" under promoted warnings), which matches the ADR's 4.7 typed-return claim. No const of a constructed object, no Object-method clash and no ClassDB class-name clash was found (checked: get, set, call, free, hash, name, script, ~70 method and member names, ~30 class names). The ADR is Proposed with its engine facts mostly first-hand, and it should not be Accepted until E1 is fixed.:
  E1 [high, BLOCKING] Key Interfaces: `SocketRef.make/section_of/index_of` use `SOCKET_INDEX_BITS` unqualified, but the constant is declared in `LayoutIds`, not in `SocketRef`. Probed on 4.7.2: `Parse Error: Identifier "SOCKET_INDEX_BITS" not declared in the current scope` on all three lines, so `socket_ref.gd` does not load and `can_instantiate()` is false. After qualifying it, the class loads and `SocketRef.make(5,3)`=83, `section_of(83)`=5, `index_of(83)`=3.
    amendment: In § Key Interfaces write `LayoutIds.SOCKET_INDEX_BITS` in all three SocketRef bodies, or declare `const SOCKET_INDEX_BITS: int = 4` inside `SocketRef` and delete it from `LayoutIds`. Prefer the second, because the constant is private to the packing. Either way, add `socket_ref.gd` and `layout_ids.gd` to the `load_all` parse gate (ADR-0010 § 5.2) as the first Layout stories.
  E2 [medium] Key Interfaces result records are written as `class_name BuildResult extends RefCounted:  var section_id: int; var body_id: int` (same for AttachResult and DetachResult). The trailing colon after the superclass is invalid GDScript. Probed: `Parse Error: Expected end of statement after superclass, found ":" instead`. The section claims "Signatures are the contract", so a story author who copies it gets a parse error.
    amendment: Rewrite as three-line files: `class_name BuildResult extends RefCounted` / `var section_id: int = 0` / `var body_id: int = 0`. Give every field an explicit default, because the fields are reused caller-owned records and ADR-0010 sets ENUM/UNTYPED warnings to errors. State once that each record resets itself through a `reset()` method (not an `_init` re-run) before every Layout fill.
  E3 [medium] § 11 says records are "get-only `RefCounted` classes", but the same records are caller-owned `out` objects that `*_into(...)` must fill (`DoorPassage`, `LeafObstruction`, `AttachPreview`, `WeldPlan`, `SectionBases`...). GDScript has no friend or internal access. A get-only property (`var x: int: get = ...`) cannot be written by another class, so either every field is a plain public `var` (consumers can write it) or each record needs a public `fill_*`/setter method. A property getter is also a function call per read (extra cost in `## @hot` paths). Tier C immutable records have the same issue for their constructor path.
    amendment: Decide per record kind. (a) `out` records: plain typed `var` fields, documented as "written only by Layout, read by the caller", with the write restriction enforced by an ADR-0010 lint (a new LAY-* row) because the language cannot. (b) Tier C returned records: set in `_init(...)` (or a static `make`) and expose fields as plain `var` read by convention, or use getters only where the cold path does not matter. Remove "get-only" from § 11 unless it is defined as lint-enforced.
  E4 [medium] Packed arrays are shared by reference in GDScript (probed: `var t := s; t[0]=99` changes `s[0]`; only `duplicate()` separates them). `AttachResult.moved_sections`, `DetachResult.moved_sections` and `rects` are caller-owned, reused packed arrays, and § 7 has Layout traverse with preallocated `PackedInt32Array` stack/visited columns in `LayoutDerived`. Two hazards. (1) If an implementation writes `out.moved_sections = <LayoutDerived column or local>` the caller now aliases Layout's scratch and the next apply silently rewrites it. (2) Anything that retains a result array across calls (Assembly's transaction log, events, Body's rebase bookkeeping) sees it change. Also, "allocation-free" is not guaranteed by `clear()` then `push_back()`: from the engine's CowData design, `resize(0)`/`clear()` releases the buffer, so a reused array that is cleared each call reallocates (UNVERIFIED on 4.7.2; the reference has no core module, and transient allocation is invisible to `Performance.MEMORY_STATIC` per ADR-0010 P7).
    amendment: Add to § 7/§ 9 and the Guidelines: result and traversal arrays are filled in place only (`resize` once at setup, write by index with a separate `count` int; never assign another array to a result field); a result is valid until the next Layout call, and any retaining consumer must `duplicate()`. For traversal stacks use fixed-length arrays plus an explicit top index rather than `clear()`/`push_back()`. Mark the no-realloc property UNVERIFIED and attach it to spike S1 (V3).
  E5 [medium] § 10 restore reads columns out of `data` (`Dictionary` of `Variant`s) into typed fields. Probed on 4.7.2: `var x: int = d["k"]` with a String value raises `Trying to assign value of type 'String' to a variable of type 'int'` and aborts the function (it returns the default); a missing key raises `Invalid access to property or key`. Inside `restore` that abort means `return ctx.complete()` is never reached and no `ctx.fault` is raised, so a corrupt column becomes an engine script error rather than `LAYOUT_RESTORE_SCHEMA`. The validate order in § 10 step (1) checks "declared type" but does not say how without a typed assignment. For the `Array[String]` column, `LayoutState.template_id = data[...]` also fails (or aliases) if the incoming array is untyped: ADR-0006 says type preservation is not asserted, and it forbids assigning an untyped Array to a typed one.
    amendment: In § 10 step (1) specify the idiom: `has()` for every key, then `typeof(v) == TYPE_PACKED_INT32_ARRAY` / `TYPE_PACKED_BYTE_ARRAY` / `TYPE_PACKED_INT64_ARRAY` / `TYPE_ARRAY` / `TYPE_DICTIONARY` before any typed assignment (ADR-0005 P20 typed-assignment idiom, not `as`). Validate each `template_id` element with `typeof(e) == TYPE_STRING`, then fill the typed column with `Array[String].assign(src)` (never plain assignment); copy packed columns with `duplicate()` into the scratch. Add that every early return path is `return ctx.complete()` after `ctx.fault(...)`. Add a fixture: a `template_id` column holding an int, and one with a missing `welds` key, each yields a named fault and writes nothing.
  E6 [low] Interaction with ADR-0010's promoted warnings (all `debug/gdscript/warnings/*` = 2), probed with `unused_parameter` and `shadowed_variable*` at 2. (a) The `@abstract` port declarations with unused parameters load cleanly (this answers ADR-0010's UNVERIFIED about UNUSED_PARAMETER on abstract methods). Concrete implementations do not: `The parameter "out" is never used in the function "section_counts_into()"`, fixed by `_out`; the renamed override still loads. (b) The Class A checks `can_build/can_attach/can_detach/can_discard(views, ...)` will not use `views` when they read Layout's own tables, so they need `_views`. (c) Methods named `version`, `static_version`, `leaf_version`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `section_at`, `rects_in` collide with natural local or parameter names inside the same class. Probed: `The local function parameter "version" is shadowing an already-declared function`. The hook bump code (`version += 1`) and ADR-0014's `@abstract func version(...)` implementer will hit it. `V` is also the only non-snake_case method name.
    amendment: Add a Guidelines bullet: unused abstract-port and check parameters are `_`-prefixed in implementations (`_views`), and locals that mirror a view method name use a different identifier (`ver`, `leaf_ver`, `new_version`). Consider renaming `V` to `room_volume_tiles` (ADR-0011's `RoomSource` already uses it) so that adapter and view share one name, or keep `V` as the GDD name and add `room_volume_tiles` as the exact method.
  E7 [low] Element writes into narrow packed columns truncate silently, with no error. Probed: `PackedByteArray[0] = 300` reads 44; `PackedInt32Array[0] = 0xDEADBEEF` and `append(4294967295)` read -559038737 and -1. The ADR relies on this deliberately for the three hashes, which is fine, but the same truncation applies to `socket_index`/`state`/`rot_q` bytes and to every int32 id/offset/base column. Counters and ids are guarded by `can_*`, yet restore (§ 10) range-checks only ids and `rot_q`, so a corrupted byte column holding e.g. 259 would decode as the legal enum 3 after a round trip.
    amendment: In § 10 step (1) and (6) state that byte columns are range-checked against their enum on the decoded value before any narrowing write (`state` in 0..1 for bodies, 1..3 for sockets, 0..2 for welds; `discarded` in 0..1; `socket_index < template.socket_count`), and that int32 columns are range-checked against int32 only where the source is an `int` outside a packed array (it cannot occur from a packed source). Add a corrupt-column fixture for a socket `state` of 259.
  E8 [info] V2 plausibility: a throwaway loop shaped like the hook (48 doors, one virtual port call with a caller-owned out object, clamp, integer floor_div through a static call, compare and store) ran at about 19 microseconds per 48 doors on the 4.7.2 mono editor binary, headless, debug. That is roughly 10x under the 0.2 ms line at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` 48. It is not a release-export figure and does not include the section-flagging and key marking, so V2 stays UNVERIFIED, but the target is not at risk from the arithmetic. The same probe shows an abstract-method dispatch plus a `RefCounted` out object costs little at this count.
    amendment: Keep V2 as is. Add this probe as the baseline to compare in the S1 spike, and record that the hook is dominated by the port call (one per door), not by the integer math, so the ADR-0010 § 9 ladder should try the Graph-change-counter early-out (OQ-5) before any native rung.
  E9 [low] Guidelines and Validation say hot reads must "never allocate" and cite a flat `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT`. As ADR-0010 P6/P7 record, OBJECT_COUNT counts only Objects, so an allocated `PackedInt32Array`, `Array`, `Dictionary` or string in `room_at`, `section_at`, `door_passage_into`, `leaf_would_overlap` or the hook is invisible to that check, and `MEMORY_STATIC` is blind to transient allocation. The only real guard is HOT-01 (lexical).
    amendment: In Validation Criteria say that allocation-freedom of the Tier H reads is enforced by HOT-01 (lexical scan of the `## @hot` bodies, which already bans `.resize(`, `.duplicate(`, literals and `PackedXArray(`) plus CNT-01 for leaked Objects only, and add the explicit list of Tier H functions to the ADR-0010 HOT-01 tag list. Do not describe OBJECT_COUNT as proving no packed-array or string allocation.
  
  ADR-0013 review verdict CONCERNS. The core decisions are sound and right-sized for a solo MVP. They are: instances by reference with dense SoA columns, dense ids with id == row + 1, the Layout/Graph id split, the lower-body_id weld survivor, a reserved idx space, and the third structure_hash, which has a concrete failing scenario behind it. The engine version is stamped (4.7.2, MEDIUM risk), and both 4.7 rows that apply (packed-array element writes and the typed-return override) are flagged. V1 is probed and V2 to V5 are named as UNVERIFIED. The alternatives were genuinely considered, and the Consequences section is honest about touch_serial churn, the LEAF family and the harsh refusal of reordered templates. Marking the LEAF key from the HOOK scope is legal under ADR-0003 (open_for in HOOK) and ADR-0004 section 7 (a mark is not a diff). TR traceability is complete: all 35 rows tagged ADR-0013 are addressed (20 decided, 12 shared, 3 owned elsewhere). Three items block Accept: (T1) the drift-policy hash rewrite inside restore() contradicts ADR-0006 SL-12's closed set of REBASED causes; (T2) the contiguous-range verification and reverse lookup ignore the HULL_SEGMENT stub rows that a RAGGED cut appends; (T3) the setup/port injection cycle with the Graph is unresolved, and the RoomSource port that ADR-0011 depends on is not declared.:
  T1 [HIGH, BLOCKING] Section 10's drift policy rewrites an instance's stored geometry_hash or visual_hash inside restore() when it accepts geometry_changed_fresh or visual_changed. The section then says the resulting K-4 state_hash mismatch is reported 'as a diagnostic, as designed'. That is false under ADR-0006 and the Save/Load GDD SL-12. A rewritten hash makes snapshot(restore(x)) != x. The five REBASED causes are a closed set (migration, retired strip, default fill, hash_algo, a REBASE_BLOCKS member), and none of them covers an owner-side content-drift rewrite. ADR-0016 section 9.3 says the case is 'accepted as a REBASED case' but names no cause. In EXACT mode the result is NOT_REPRODUCED, which halts dev and test builds and marks the generation suspect in release. A visual-only art tweak to a section template, the most common edit before release, would therefore halt every dev load of every existing save.
    amendment: Make restore() byte-identical. Never rewrite a stored hash in restore(): keep the stored values in LayoutState, raise geometry_changed_fresh or visual_changed (re-raised on each load until the instance changes), and re-derive the rects from the current template, which already happens because rects are derived. Refresh an instance's three stored hashes from the current template inside LM2 attach_section, the moment the instance first gets history. The history-dependent geometry rule then compares against the template that history was made under, and a later weld cannot cause a false refusal. Strike the sentence ending 'as designed'. Add a Validation criterion: after a visual-only and after a fresh-geometry template edit, the load verifies EXACT/MATCH. If this is rejected, the alternative is an ADR-0006 amendment that adds a sixth REBASED cause (content drift accepted) reported through ctx. That option costs more.
  T2 [HIGH, BLOCKING] Section 3 and section 10 (d) assume each section's Graph ids are exactly the contiguous ranges [node_base, node_base + template count). The post-restore check 'node, edge and compartment counts match the template' is described as a pure comparison, and the reverse lookup from Graph id to section is a bsearch over node_base. ADR-0011 sections 3.6 and 4.1 (3) say a RAGGED cut_detach appends the hull stubs as ordinary HULL_SEGMENT node rows, flagged STUB, with fresh high ids, and discard_section tombstones every row of a section. If section_counts_into counts by section_id, every save made after a RAGGED cut fails Layout's post_restore and takes LOADING to FAULTED. If it does not, the bsearch reverse lookup still answers NONE for a stub id. anchor_geometry and plate_positions then return nothing for a leaking stub that Failure & Trail and the Emitter's fault glow need to place.
    amendment: Define check (d) precisely. For each non-discarded instance, the rows in [node_base, node_base + template.node_count) and the matching edge range resolve to section s and are not tombstoned, and compartment k == comp_base + k. Rows outside the template range (STUB rows, seam edges) are excluded. For a discarded instance, the same ranges resolve to tombstones of section s. State in section 3 that the bsearch mapping covers template-range ids only. Stub nodes resolve through GraphView.section_of(id) plus the seam's stub list, and anchor_geometry for a stub answers the cut socket's hatch span, or explicitly NONE with a named owner for its placement. Add a fixture: RAGGED cut, save, restore, verify passes and anchor_geometry(stub) is as specified.
  T3 [MEDIUM, BLOCKING] The construction order is circular and incompletely declared. architecture.md section 8 sets up Layout before the Graph. LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning, graph: LayoutGraphPort) needs the Graph facade, but GraphModule.setup(facet, tuning, catalog, rooms: RoomSource, strict_numeric) runs later and needs a RoomSource that ADR-0011 says 'Layout's read view implements'. ADR-0013 never mentions RoomSource (room_volume_tiles and room_exposed_tiles, -1 for an unknown room). Its read_view facade is put at registry freeze, which is after both setups. A Layout story cannot be written against this.
    amendment: In section 1 and Key Interfaces, state that LayoutViews is constructed inside LayoutModule.setup and lives for the whole process, and that it implements ADR-0011's @abstract RoomSource (exposed as layout.room_source() for the composition root). List room_volume_tiles and room_exposed_tiles in section 11 Tier H with their sentinels. Break the cycle explicitly, for example with a LayoutModule.bind_graph(port: LayoutGraphPort) that the composition root calls after GraphModule.setup and before the registry freeze. Port calls before the freeze are a defect (asserted). Then update the architecture.md section 8 step 4 note.
  T4 [MEDIUM] LayoutGraphPort has drifted from the Graph side. The port says check_instantiate and SectionBases; ADR-0011 and ADR-0012 say check_instantiate_section and InstantiateResult. Section 3's table lists a 'comp counter in graph.state', but ADR-0011 has four counters and comp_base == node_base because compartments are COMPARTMENT nodes. Section 3 and section 7 (LM2) read seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids, which bypasses the port that section 8 calls Layout's only route to the Graph. Section 8 says opening_into is valid 'in P3 and in P2', but LM1 seeds leaves in the INIT scope of init_world. can_build's closed reason set maps any Graph refusal to CAPACITY, yet check_instantiate_section can return ONSET_UNKEYED and the other LS-18 reasons.
    amendment: Rename the port members to ADR-0011's names (InstantiateResult, check_instantiate_section). Change the section 3 compartment row to 'COMPARTMENT node ids; comp_base == node_base (ADR-0011 section 4.4)'. Replace both seam_view references with seam_openings_into. Add INIT to the scopes where the port reads are valid. State that can_build passes a Graph reason through as layout.GRAPH_<REASON>, or that the reason is unreachable at runtime because the ADR-0007 template validator calls graph_rules.onset_valid at boot.
  T5 [MEDIUM] Section 11 does not list reads that Core siblings have already built on. ADR-0015 needs body_is_live(body_id) and section_contains(section_id, x, y). ADR-0017 E1 needs node_base(section_id) and an emitter-placement accessor on SectionTemplate (def_id, anchor, node_ordinal, switch_on, subkind); section 4 names only fixture_anchors and instrument_placements. ADR-0014 needs the RectFlags bit values and file and the SlotFeed (slot_count, slot_footprint, slot_extent), and it adds section_rects_into, which is keyed by section but answers in the body frame. That breaks this ADR's frame rule in section 5 and section 11 ('Every geometry read answers section-local'; 'A read never mixes frames') unless the rule is amended.
    amendment: Add a 'Reads owed to Core siblings' table to section 11 with exact signatures and tiers: body_is_live, section_contains, node_base/edge_base/comp_base getters, SectionTemplate.emitter_placement_* idx accessors, src/sim/layout/rect_flags.gd with its bit values and ALL mask, and the SlotFeed. Add section_rects_into to the section 5 list of body-frame reads as the one section-keyed exception.
  T6 [LOW] Section 13 closes the kind_ordinal vocabulary at six kinds (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar), but section 5 reserves a JAMB variant slot for every hatched socket, TR-assembly-045 names jambs, and ADR-0034 assigns JAMB 7 (its OQ-C).
    amendment: Add JAMB to the section 13 closed vocabulary. Ordinal values stay ADR-0034's.
  T7 [LOW] The version-counter text predates ADR-0014. Section 10 says the restore resets counters to 1 and that 'every rebuilding consumer rebuilds on tick 1', and that every section reports changed_region ALL once after a restore. ADR-0014 (section 6) shows the ALL stamp is not guaranteed to be seen. It makes version_epoch the authoritative restore signal and replaces LM4's bump with invalidate (all three counters set to 0). Section 9's LM4 row states no version effect at all.
    amendment: In section 9 (LM4) and section 10, adopt ADR-0014's invalidate on discard and new_epoch() on restore/default_state. Cite version_epoch as the consumer rebuild signal, and demote 'changed_region ALL after restore' to a non-guaranteed hint.
  T8 [LOW] Section 10 post_restore (a) contradicts itself: 'an area above area_max is clamped with a diagnostic, and the same fault found here is LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING'. One case cannot be both a clamp-and-continue and a fault that takes LOADING to FAULTED.
    amendment: Follow TR-section-035: in post_restore an area above area_max is LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING via ctx.fault (no clamp). In the layout.doors hook it is clamped with area_clamped.
  T9 [LOW] Weld canonicalisation stops at layout.state. socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b) fills the Graph's JoinPlan in argument order, so graph.state's seam row (section_a/section_b, opening order) can differ between attach(x, y) and attach(y, x). The Consequence 'same bytes for the same world regardless of argument order, so state_hash equality and replay hold' is proved only for layout.state.
    amendment: Have socket_plan canonicalise to survivor-first through weld_math.survivor_of, so JoinPlan and opening_ids are argument-order independent. Extend the weld-symmetry Validation criterion to whole-world state_hash equality.
  T10 [LOW] Spike gating is honest in the text (V2 and V3 are pending S1 figures with ADR-0010's fallback ladder; V4 waits on ADR-0005). However, architecture.md's S1 / SP-ENG-1 row lists ADR-0012, 0014, 0015 and 0017 but not ADR-0013, and the ADR never states whether Accept is gated on S1. OQ-2 (line 1367 of requirements-traceability.md still reads ADR-0013 + ADR-0007 for TR-derelict-034) is still open.
    amendment: State in Engine Compatibility that Accept is not gated on V2/V3 (they are cost lines with a fallback, and no data shape depends on them), while V4 golden vectors gate the template-hash story. Route to /architecture-review: add ADR-0013 V2/V3 to the S1 row and fix summary line 1367.
  
  CROSS-ADR RULINGS (binding):
  CT-01 owner ADR-0011 (align: ADR-0013, ADR-0012, ADR-0016): Merges 0011-review items 1 (first half) and 7, 0013-review items 1 and 9, and ADR-0011 T4. ADR-0013 owns the `LayoutGraphPort` definition. ADR-0011 is the implementer and currently publishes nothing for it. The Graph facade cannot be `GraphModule` or `GraphView`: GDScript has single inheritance, and `GraphView` must stay a pure, getter-only view. The implementer therefore has to be a dedicated adapter class. It cannot sit under `ports/`, because ADR-0010 ARCH-05 requires every file under `ports/` to be `@abstract`. The out-type name is the port owner's: `SectionBases` wins, and `InstantiateResult` is deleted, not aliased. M1's call chain follows ADR-0013 (Web Map -> LM1 -> port), because Layout allocates `section_id` first.
    amendment: ADR-0011, new section 9.5 'Layout port' plus a Key Interfaces snippet: `class_name GraphLayoutAdapter extends LayoutGraphPort` in `src/sim/graph/graph_layout_adapter.gd` (outside `ports/`, ARCH-05). GraphModule.setup constructs it and exposes it as `graph.layout_port()`. It holds `GraphMutators` and `GraphView`, so `GraphView` keeps its pure getter-only contract. It implements all five methods with caller-owned outs and no allocation: (1) `check_instantiate_section(views, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int) -> StringName`, the pure Class A check returning the LS-18 reasons plus CAPACITY and ONSET_UNKEYED, which is the same function ADR-0012 calls `check_instantiate_section`; (2) `instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out: SectionBases) -> int`, which is M1; (3) `opening_into(edge_id, out: OpeningRead) -> bool`, with `door_state` derived from `area` (LS-19); (4) `seam_openings_into(seam_id, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool`, with `opening_ids` in `socket_plan.openings` order and valid after restore; (5) `section_counts_into(section_id, out: SectionCounts) -> bool`, which reads persisted columns only (Tier S) and follows CT-03. The reads are valid in APPLY, INIT, HOOK and post_restore. The two writers are valid in APPLY and INIT. Delete `views/instantiate_result.gd`. M1's out type is ADR-0013's `SectionBases {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` (in `src/sim/layout/views/`). Update section 11 and the interfaces registry candidate to match. In the section 1 row 'init_world, binding_source' and in section 4.4, write: 'M1's only caller is Layout LM1 through `LayoutGraphPort`; LM1's callers are those ADR-0013 section 9 names (Web Map `init_world` in the INIT scope at the MVP).' ADR-0012 section 6 (M1 row and Rules) gets the same wording. ADR-0016 section 3.4's Tier S list already names these reads and needs no change.
  CT-02 owner ADR-0013 (align: ADR-0011, ADR-0014, ADR-0015): Merges 0011-review item 1 (second half), 0013-review items 2, 11 and 12 (T3), and the RoomSource half of the LayoutViews single-inheritance item. ADR-0013 owns the port signature and the four record types. `LayoutViews` cannot extend several ports. The setup order is circular: Layout is set up first and needs the Graph port, while the Graph's setup needs Layout's `RoomSource`. I checked ADR-0010 section 2: sim-to-sim imports are allowed in any direction at module granularity, so ports that point both ways create no import-matrix problem and nothing needs to move to `src/shared/`.

- adopt: Brownfield audit — do existing artifacts actually work? Numbered migration plan. Unlike /project-stage-detect, checks compliance not existence.
- agents-sdk: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Agents SDK applications using the agents package.
- architecture-decision: Create an ADR documenting a technical decision: context, alternatives considered, consequences.
- architecture-review: Traceability matrix mapping GDD requirements to ADRs. Finds gaps, cross-ADR conflicts, engine compatibility. PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL.
- art-bible: Author the Art Bible — visual identity gating asset production. Run before /map-systems.
- asset-audit: Audit assets against naming conventions, file size budgets, format standards. Finds orphaned assets, missing references.
- asset-spec: Per-asset visual specs plus AI generation prompts from GDDs and character profiles. After the art bible.
- balance-check: Find balance outliers, broken progressions, degenerate strategies, economy imbalances in formulas and data. 'Check game balance'.
- basin: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare Basin analytics workflows with Basin Pipelines, Basin Catalog, and Basin SQL. Use for streaming data into R2 Iceberg tables, managing catalogs, or querying those tables; also use for requests using the former Data Platform, Pipelines, R2 Data Catalog, or R2 SQL names.
- brainstorm: Guided concept ideation using professional studio techniques, player psychology, creative exploration.
- brownfield: First-principles audit and improvement plan for an EXISTING codebase ("brownfield" project) — especially one the user can run and demo but can't confidently judge. Orchestrates parallel specialist subagents (architecture, product-intent, code, tests, security, performance, docs) that treat existing code as evidence rather than ground truth, keeps an assumptions register and escalates the risky ones, writes a consolidated improvement design doc with a dependency-ordered PR plan sized to the repo, runs a writer↔reviewer loop until no critical/major issues remain, and optionally (--execute) implements the plan as worktree-isolated, reviewed git branches. Use this skill whenever the user says /brownfield, asks to audit / health-check / assess / sanity-check / "second opinion" an existing repo or legacy app, asks "is this built correctly?", "what's wrong with this codebase?", "a contractor/AI built this and I'm not sure it's right", wants a prioritized improvement or remediation plan for code that already exists, or is inheriting a project and wants to know where the bodies are buried — even if they never use the word "brownfield". Not for greenfield design of new systems or for reviewing a single small diff/PR.
- bug-report: Structured bug report from a description, or analyze code for potential bugs. Reproduction steps, severity.
- bug-triage: Re-evaluate open bugs — priority vs severity, assign to sprints, surface systemic trends. Run when the count grows.
- ccgs-code-review: Architectural code review — coding standards, SOLID, testability, performance concerns.
- changelog: Auto-generate a changelog from git commits and sprint data. Internal and player-facing versions.
- cloudflare: Discover and choose Cloudflare products for apps, APIs, AI agents, storage, networking, and security. Use for architecture and product selection, including when the user describes a need without naming a Cloudflare product; then find the relevant skill or documentation.
- cloudflare-email-service: Implement or troubleshoot Cloudflare Email Sending and Email Routing integrations and their delivery configuration.
- cloudflare-one: Design, configure, troubleshoot, or review Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE deployments. Use cloudflare-one-migrations for migration planning from other vendors.
- cloudflare-one-migrations: Assess and plan migrations from existing VPN, SWG, or SASE platforms to Cloudflare One, including policy mapping, parity gaps, and rollout.
- code-review: Review a branch, PR, commit range, or working tree with separate Standards and Spec tasks through review_run. Use when the user asks for a code review or asks to review changes since a fixed point.
- consistency-check: Scan GDDs against the entity registry for cross-document conflicts. Grep-first approach targets conflicting sections, different stats.
- content-audit: Audit GDD content counts against what's implemented — planned vs built.
- create-architecture: Author the architecture blueprint before code is written. Validates decisions against the pinned engine, flags knowledge gaps.
- create-control-manifest: Flat must-do/never-do rules sheet per system and layer, extracted from Accepted ADRs. ADRs explain why; this is actionable.
- create-epics: Turn GDDs plus architecture into epics — one per architectural module, with untraced requirements. Then /create-stories [epic-slug].
- create-stories: Break one epic into implementable stories embedding TR-ID, ADR guidance, acceptance criteria. Reads the control manifest. After /create-epics.
- design-review: Reviews one design document for completeness, internal consistency, implementability, and design standards. Before handing to programmers.
- design-system: Section-by-section GDD authoring for one system — walks through each required section, cross-references dependencies.
- durable-objects: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Durable Objects code for persistent state and coordination.
- estimate: Estimate task effort from complexity, dependencies, velocity, risk. Structured estimate with confidence levels.
- gate-check: Ready to advance between development phases? PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL with blockers and required artifacts. 'Can we move to production?'
- help: What should I do next? Use when stuck or you don't know what to do.

- milestone-review: Milestone progress review — completeness, quality metrics, risk, go/no-go recommendation. At checkpoints or before a deadline.

For setup, migration, or deployment, install vinext's upstream skills with `npx skills add cloudflare/vinext` if missing, then read and follow the applicable skill and docs.

Orchestrates parallel specialist subagents (architecture, product-intent, code, tests, security, performance, docs) that treat existing code as evidence rather than ground truth, keeps an assumptions register and escalates the risky ones, writes a consolidated improvement design doc with a dependency-ordered PR plan sized to the repo, runs a writer↔reviewer loop until no critical/major issues remain, and optionally (--execute) implements the plan as worktree-isolated, reviewed git branches. Use this skill whenever the user says /brownfield, asks to audit / health-check / assess / sanity-check / "second opinion" an existing repo or legacy app, asks "is this built correctly?", "what's wrong with this codebase?", "a contractor/AI built this and I'm not sure it's right", wants a prioritized improvement or remediation plan for code that already exists, or is inheriting a project and wants to know where the bodies are buried — even if they never use the word "brownfield". # Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Godot Engine — Version Reference

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine Version** | Godot 4.7 |
| **Installed at pin time** | 4.7.2.stable.mono.official.ed1daf0bf (matches pin; probed 2026-10-25 at `C:/Users/dasbl/Documents/Godot/`). 4.6.2 standard is also installed, unused. |
| **Release Date** | June 2026 (latest patch: 4.7.2, August 2026) |
| **Project Pinned** | 2026-10-17 |
| **Last Docs Verified** | 2026-10-17 (release timeline and 4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (4.4-4.6 content) |
| **LLM Knowledge Cutoff** | May 2025 |

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

## Post-Cutoff Version Timeline

| Version | Release | Risk Level | Key Theme |
|---------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 4.5 | Sep 2025 | HIGH | Accessibility (AccessKit), variadic args, @abstract, shader baker, SMAA |
| 4.6 | Jan 2026 | HIGH | Jolt default, glow rework, D3D12 default on Windows, IK restored |
| 4.7 | Jun 2026 | HIGH | AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store replaces the Asset Library, VirtualJoystick, Jolt soft-body and world-boundary changes, typed-return overrides |

## Before the Cutoff

4.4 (Mar 2025, Jolt option, FileAccess return types) predates the May 2025
cutoff; the Knowledge Gap Warning still applies to it.

Dates from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases, checked 2026-10-17:
4.4 Mar 3 2025, 4.5 Sep 15 2025, 4.6 Jan 26 2026, 4.7 Jun 18 2026, 4.7.2 Aug 18
2026. Migration guides and release notes: `breaking-changes.md` § Sources.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag
- [Consistency-check needs a confirming run](consistency-check-confirming-run.md) — owner+registry fixes leave leftovers in consumer GDDs; grep referenced_by docs, print patch counts

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.
</system-reminder>
